newsitem.title: USA: Snow falls in Amarillo, rain in Oklahoma - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Snow falls in Amarillo, rain in Oklahoma - WSC.

text.p: Rain turned to snow in the Texas Panhandle, with about one inch on the ground in Amarillo early Friday, said Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio.
Temperatures dipped to 32 degrees Fahrenheit in Amarillo, a record low there for this date, Burgio said. The snow should turn back to rain later Friday for the Panhandle.
"They will see rain and thundershowers today, which should total another one to two inches (near Amarillo), and two to four inches in the eastern Texas Panhandle and southwest Oklahoma," he said.
Localized flash flooding was likely in the areas of heaviest rain, said Burgio.

Light showers fell in southern Kansas, with about 0.25 inch in the southwest section and less than 0.1 elsewhere. For the next 24 hours, 0.3 to 1.0 inch were forecast for south central and southeast Kansas, and 0.1 to 0.5 inch in southwest and northeast Kansas.

The storm system now in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma should move east reaching Arkansas and northern Louisiana late Saturday and early Sunday. Rain amounts of 0.5 to 2.0 inches were forecast there.
"Western and southern Arkansas, northern Louisiana and southern Mississippi could get two inches or more," said Burgio.
Except for some scattered showers in southern and far eastern Midwest, most Midwest corn and soybean areas should remain dry, but soils will remain cool through the weekend.
"You could plant if you want to," said Burgio.
The cool Midwest weather should be replaced Wednesday by warmer conditions.

Light showers of 0.1 to 0.5 inch were likely in the eastern Dakotas Friday, which should not add to the flooding, he said. The rest of the northern Plains should remain dry through the weekend, said Burgio.
